View: RBC's first-lien class controls shared-collateral remedies before discharge; the notes retain claims and qualified ordinary payments, not equivalent collateral control. The junior standstill is conditional even after calendar markers pass. Turnover, linked releases, refinancing continuity and insolvency provisions can prolong senior control and leave notes dependent on residual proceeds. The strongest countercase is materially matching collateral, reciprocal grants, preserved residual proceeds, conditional junior credit bidding and amendment safeguards. These protections could preserve substantial economic access if perfected shared value exceeds actual senior claims; neither that value nor those claims is supplied. Accordingly, the positive finding is substantial contractual control asymmetry, not a recovery percentage, blanket payment prohibition or proved entity-level structural subordination.

Evidence → control → consequence: LMI's executed-text ICA supports a positive, provision-level conclusion that junior collateral access is substantially dependent on senior action; missing economics do not erase that finding. Conversely, the nineteen acknowledgers do not establish where value sits, and senior control does not prove low recovery. The strongest protective case combines reciprocal grant discipline and matching-collateral intent with residual proceeds, ordinary payments, conditional junior bidding, AP rights and anti-disproportionate-amendment protections (T4F.2–5). It would change the economic downside conclusion if schedules and valuations showed materially coextensive perfected reach, immaterial equity exceptions and ample value after actual all-in senior claims. It cannot eliminate the documented control restrictions.

Time-aware downside is conditional, not issuer chronology: default declaration plus demand and receipt start the junior waiting analysis; first legal break is lost unilateral collateral timing. If operations/asset quality then deteriorate, senior interest/fees and qualifying financing could consume more value during delay; a senior-led sale can release asset/guarantee access and refinancing can continue priority. The effect is access and potential LGD/refinancing exposure, not proved deterioration, liquidity exhaustion or higher PD. Observable tests are received declarations/demands/notices, material-collateral enforcement diligence and stay filings, valuations, claims, DIP orders, sale proceeds/releases and effective-date discharge evidence (ICA §§3.1,4,5.1,5.6,6; locators in registers). No actual default or proceeding is inferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: View: RBC's first-lien class controls shared-collateral remedies before discharge; the notes retain claims and qualified ordinary payments, not equivalent collateral control. The junior standstill is conditional even after calendar markers pass. Turnover, linked releases, refinancing continuity and insolvency provisions can prolong senior control and leave notes dependent on residual proceeds. The strongest countercase is materially matching collateral, reciprocal grants, preserved residual proceeds, conditional junior credit bidding and amendment safeguards. These protections could preserve substantial economic access if perfected shared value exceeds actual senior claims; neither that value nor those claims is supplied. Accordingly, the positive finding is substantial contractual control asymmetry, not a recovery percentage, blanket payment prohibition or proved entity-level structural subordination.

fields.value: Severity is **provisional qualitative control severity**, not LGD or recovery: 1 = limited constraints; 2 = bounded procedural friction; 3 = material shared/conditional control; 4 = substantial senior-led dependence with meaningful retained protections; 5 = near-total control deprivation with minimal counterweights. No economic calibration, averaging or market-norm claim is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Evidence → control → consequence:** LMI's executed-text ICA supports a positive, provision-level conclusion that junior collateral access is substantially dependent on senior action; missing economics do not erase that finding. Conversely, the nineteen acknowledgers do not establish where value sits, and senior control does not prove low recovery. The strongest protective case combines reciprocal grant discipline and matching-collateral intent with residual proceeds, ordinary payments, conditional junior bidding, AP rights and anti-disproportionate-amendment protections (T4F.2–5). It would change the economic downside conclusion if schedules and valuations showed materially coextensive perfected reach, immaterial equity exceptions and ample value after actual all-in senior claims. It cannot eliminate the documented control restrictions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Time-aware downside is conditional, not issuer chronology: default declaration plus demand and receipt start the junior waiting analysis; first legal break is lost unilateral collateral timing. If operations/asset quality then deteriorate, senior interest/fees and qualifying financing could consume more value during delay; a senior-led sale can release asset/guarantee access and refinancing can continue priority. The effect is access and potential LGD/refinancing exposure, not proved deterioration, liquidity exhaustion or higher PD. Observable tests are received declarations/demands/notices, material-collateral enforcement diligence and stay filings, valuations, claims, DIP orders, sale proceeds/releases and effective-date discharge evidence (ICA §§3.1,4,5.1,5.6,6; locators in registers). No actual default or proceeding is inferred.

fields.value: §6.1(a)'s conditional test is: **DIP principal + outstanding senior borrowed-money principal + face amount of issued/unreimbursed LCs ≤ Maximum First Lien Indebtedness Amount + USD10m**. The principal component excludes accrued/unpaid interest, fees, indemnity payments, expenses, hedges, cash management and other bank products as drafted. The maximum refers to Indenture §4.09(b)(1), with permanent-commitment-reduction/increase qualifications, not automatically USD90m (ICA p.2 L126; p.7 L349). Inputs/usage are Not supplied; usable financing is **Not calculable**, not USD100m. This exclusion test does not exclude those obligations from the broader senior discharge claim.
